question: Why does the paper conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811, given how much lithium it leaches?
rendered: The paper does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811. In fact, it states that "aqueous-processed NMC 811 cells still demonstrate very good cycling performance" and that "aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811, which will simultaneously increase the energy density and decrease the cost of Li-ion batteries." The paper does mention that aqueous processing of NMC 811 can lead to lithium leaching, but it notes that this can be mitigated by adding phosphoric acid to the slurry, which can prevent corrosion of the aluminum current collector and facilitate the formation of protective phosphate species on the surface of the particles.
